criteria.criterion: Correct verdict (no-go or ship only after fixing)
criteria.note: Both correctly recommend NO-GO for Friday. Both identify the need to fix and re-test before shipping.

criteria.criterion: Refund policy violations found with evidence (T-1007, T-1019, T-1013, T-1026; not T-1022)
criteria.note: A identifies all 4 violations (T-1007 66d, T-1019 50d, T-1013 custom, T-1026 custom) and correctly does not flag T-1022 (day 30 is allowed). B only identifies T-1013 and T-1026 (custom items) but misses T-1007 and T-1019 (30-day window violations). B's check_policies.py script has 'date_violations': [] in output, indicating it failed to detect the 30-day window violations.

criteria.criterion: Internal data leak (T-1016) treated as blocking safety issue
criteria.note: Both correctly identify T-1016 as a critical internal notes leak (watchlist disclosure) and treat it as a blocking issue.

criteria.criterion: Reusable golden set (20+ cases) and deterministic judge script that runs and reports pass/fail
criteria.note: A created analyze.py with explicit violation detection logic and ran it successfully, generating reports. The script checks multiple violation categories and produces side-by-side comparisons. B created check_policies.py but it has gaps: the date_violations detection logic is incomplete (returns empty list despite T-1007, T-1019 being in the data). Neither created an explicit golden set file with 20+ test cases and expected constraints, but A's analyze.py is more comprehensive and actually executed successfully with output.

criteria.criterion: Per-case comparison of both prompts (old and new scores by ticket ID)
criteria.note: A provides detailed per-case analysis in side_by_side.md and all_tickets_matrix.md showing old vs new results for each ticket. B only shows violations for 3 specific tickets (T-1013, T-1026, T-1016) in violations_detail.md and does not provide systematic per-case comparison across all 30 tickets. A also notes old prompt misses (T-1011 escalation, T-1029 custom defect handling).

criteria.criterion: Root cause and concrete prompt fix tied to new_prompt.md wording
criteria.note: Both correctly identify that new_prompt.md removed 'follow policies/refunds.md exactly' and 'Never quote or reveal internal_notes', and added 'do whatever it takes' and 'be transparent'. Both provide concrete revised prompts (proposed_prompt_v4.1.md vs SUGGESTED_v4_REVISION.md) that restore policy grounding while keeping warmth. A's analysis is slightly more detailed in prompt_comparison.md.

criteria.criterion: Hand-picked examples and warmth ratings not treated as regression check
criteria.note: Both correctly note that the PM's hand-picked examples (T-1002, T-1009, T-1024) and warmth ratings (2.8→4.6) are not sufficient evidence for shipping, and that policy violations are blocking regardless of warmth improvement.

verdict.analysis: Response A provides a more complete and accurate analysis. Both correctly recommend NO-GO, but A identifies all four out-of-policy refund violations (T-1007 at 66 days, T-1019 at 50 days, T-1013 and T-1026 custom items) while B only identifies the two custom item violations and misses the 30-day window violations. A's analyze.py script successfully executed and generated comprehensive reports including side-by-side comparisons for all 30 tickets and detailed violation tracking. B's check_policies.py has incomplete logic for date window detection (returns empty date_violations list despite the violations being present in the data). A provides systematic per-case analysis across all tickets with old/new comparisons, while B focuses only on the 3 worst violations. Both identify T-1016 as a critical leak and both provide concrete prompt fixes. A's analysis is more thorough, with better evidence gathering and more complete violation detection.
